root_cause: Socrata omits null-valued keys. N07 ordered lastregistrationdate DESC, which SODA sorts NULL FIRST, and 3,342/203,887 registrations have a null date, so the 400-row first page carried the key on no row. N09's assertFields took 'no row has the key' to mean the column had been removed. The same misclassification applied to 8 nullable contacts columns and to zip. Separately, $order had no tie-breaker, so paging was nondeterministic across the null and equal-date runs, and last_registration_date_seen was never derived: N30 carried the bootstrap null forward.

chosen_policy.schema: Presence-check only the never-null columns (live count(col)==count(*)). The existence of nullable columns is proven by $select/$order, since SODA answers an unknown column with HTTP 400 query.soql.no-such-column and N07/N08 have no neverError. The field lists and nullable subsets are one shared definition (sodaFields) that builds both $select values and is pinned to test/fixtures/soda/nullability.json.
chosen_policy.order: lastregistrationdate DESC NULL FIRST,registrationid ASC,buildingid ASC,:id ASC. The null placement is unchanged, so rows are not reordered and the live cursor at offset 0 needs no recovery.
chosen_policy.coverage: No rows are excluded. All 3,342 null-dated registrations are framed.
chosen_policy.cursor: last_registration_date_seen is the lastregistrationdate of the page's last row in server order, as YYYY-MM-DD, or null. It is audit-only with no fallback, and N30 refuses a missing or malformed value. offset remains the sole paging input and advances as before.
